listing.description: The listing in the marketplace's own JSON format (for Etsy, Open API v3 style snake_case fields; for Amazon, title, brand, bullet_points, description, search_terms, product_type, price, quantity, images). Must be a JSON object.

marketplace.description: Marketplace code, case-insensitive. Supported: ETSY, AMAZON.

analysisVersion.description: Version of the whole analysis that produced the result. Currently equal to rulesetVersion; it will also change when other analyzers (for example an LLM step) are added. Two checks with the same marketplace, contentHash and analysisVersion have the same result.

cached.description: True when an identical listing had already been checked with the same analysisVersion and the stored result is returned instead of a new check.

checkId.description: Identifier of the stored check; use it with GET /api/v1/checks/{id}.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the normalized listing content.

createdAt.description: When the check was first stored.

fixesComputed.description: Whether verified fixes were computed for this result.

readiness.description: Readiness from the listing-rules pack only; null when this legacy result has not been enriched.

rulesetVersion.description: Version of the ruleset that produced the findings. Null for checks stored before versions were recorded.

field.description: Field path, see the integration guide.

fix.description: A verified suggestion for this finding; null when no certain fix exists.

message.example: Tag 'a tag that is far too long...' dài 38 ký tự, tối đa 20.

suggestion.example: Rút ngắn tag này ít nhất 18 ký tự.

value.description: The value that caused the finding; null when no single value applies (a missing field).
value.example: a tag that is far too long for the limit

enabled.description: False when the rule is switched off for this product type: nothing is enforced and the number is only on record. A counter should not enforce a limit that is not enabled.

field.description: The field of the standard input (`docs/input-schema.md`) the limit applies to, such as `title`, `tags`, `bullet_points` or `search_terms`. For a list field, `MAX_COUNT` limits the list and `MAX_LENGTH` or `MAX_BYTES` limit each item. A field inside the Etsy `personalization` block is a path: `[]` stands for every question, and `[type=DROPDOWN]` or `[type=UPLOAD]` for the questions of that type, for example `personalization.questions[].question_text`.

kind.description: What is limited: `MAX_LENGTH` (length of a text, or of each item of a list), `MAX_COUNT` (number of items of a list, or of words of a text), `MAX_BYTES` (size in UTF-8 bytes) or `MAX_OCCURRENCES` (how often the same word or character may appear).

ruleId.description: The rule that enforces the limit; the `ruleId` of its findings.

severity.description: How a finding that breaks the limit is rated.

sourceStatus.description: How well the number is backed by the marketplace's documentation: `VERIFIED`, `SECONDARY` or `UNVERIFIED`.

unit.description: What is counted, as the rule counts it: `CODE_POINTS` (an emoji counts once, not the UTF-16 length of a JavaScript string), `ITEMS`, `WORDS`, `UTF8_BYTES` or `OCCURRENCES`.

limits.description: Every numeric limit of the ruleset's rules, in rule order. A rule that is switched off is listed with `enabled` false. Read the limits you need by `field` and `kind`, and ignore the ones you do not know.

marketplace.description: The marketplace code, in upper case.

productType.description: The product type asked for, trimmed and as sent; null when none was asked for.

rulesetVersion.description: The version of the ruleset the limits come from; the same value as `rulesetVersion` of a check. Opaque: compare for equality, do not parse.

analysisVersion.description: Version of everything that decides the result (ruleset, algorithms, catalog, database). Opaque: compare for equality only. Two checks of one client with the same marketplace, the same listing text and the same analysisVersion have the same result.

cached.description: True when the stored result of an identical earlier check is returned instead of a new analysis. Only a COMPLETE result is ever returned from the cache.

catalogVersion.description: Version of the trademark catalog the text was compared with. Opaque.

checkId.description: Identifier of the stored check; use it with GET /api/v1/trademark-checks/{id} until expiresAt.

completeness.description: COMPLETE when every rule ran. INCOMPLETE when a rule failed: the findings of the rules that succeeded are kept, failedRuleIds names the others, and riskLevel is the highest established level or UNKNOWN.

createdAt.description: When the check was first stored (UTC).

disclaimer.description: Statement that the result is a reference warning and not a legal conclusion. Show it with the result.

expiresAt.description: When the stored result stops being readable (UTC). After this instant GET answers 404 and the same listing is analysed again.

failedRuleIds.description: Rules that failed; empty for a COMPLETE result.

riskLevel.description: The highest level among the findings (LOW when a complete check found nothing above LOW). UNKNOWN means the risk could not be determined because the check is INCOMPLETE; it is never reported as LOW.

rulesetVersion.description: Version of the trademark ruleset that produced the result.

enforced.description: Whether plans are on in this deployment. When false the quota and the packs are not applied: `monthlyQuota` and `remaining` are null and `packs` lists every pack.

monthlyQuota.description: Results the plan allows per UTC month; null means unlimited. One unit is one new result that is stored, per endpoint: a cached result costs nothing, and a full check of one listing (rules and trademark) is two units.

packs.description: The packs the client may use.

periodStart.description: First day of the current UTC month.

plan.description: The client's plan code: FREE, SELLER or PRO.

remaining.description: Units left this month; null when the quota is unlimited or not applied.

resetAt.description: The instant the quota resets: the start of the next UTC month.

used.description: Units used so far in the current UTC month.

children.description: The children: objects with sku, parent_sku (Amazon only), title and attributes, a map from an attribute name to its value. Entries that are not objects or are empty are dropped.

marketplace.description: Marketplace code, case-insensitive. Supported: ETSY, AMAZON.

parent.description: Amazon: the parent, an object with sku, product_type, variation_theme and title (all optional). Ignored for Etsy, where the listing is its own parent.

variation_properties.description: Etsy: the names of the variation types, for example ["Primary color", "Size"]. Ignored for Amazon.

analysisVersion.description: Version of everything that decides the result (ruleset, comparison logic, input format). Opaque: compare for equality only. Two checks of one client with the same marketplace, the same family and the same analysisVersion have the same result.

cached.description: True when the stored result of an identical earlier check is returned instead of a new analysis. Only a COMPLETE result is ever returned from the cache.

checkId.description: Identifier of the stored check; use it with GET /api/v1/variation-checks/{id} until expiresAt.

completeness.description: COMPLETE when every rule ran. INCOMPLETE when a rule failed: the findings of the rules that succeeded are kept and failedRuleIds names the others. An INCOMPLETE result is never a clean result.

createdAt.description: When the check was first stored (UTC).

disclaimer.description: Statement that the result is a reference warning and not a statement of the marketplace. Show it with the result.

expiresAt.description: When the stored result stops being readable (UTC). After this instant GET answers 404 and the same family is analysed again.

failedRuleIds.description: Rules that failed; empty for a COMPLETE result.

rulesetVersion.description: Version of the variation ruleset that produced the result.

ApiKeyAuth.description: Service-to-service API key issued to a client. A client can hold several keys at once to allow rotation; checks, cached results and the rate limit belong to the client, not to the key.
ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key

info.description:
Checks a marketplace listing before it is published and returns findings with suggestions. It only checks and suggests: it never edits a listing and never publishes anything.

Every endpoint except GET /health needs the X-API-Key header. Errors are RFC 7807 problem responses (application/problem+json) with a stable `code`; quote the `requestId` when reporting one. See docs/integration-guide.md for the calling flow, error table and field path conventions.
info.title: Listing Guard API

post.description: Normalizes the listing, runs the marketplace's rules and stores the result. If the same listing content was already checked by the calling client with the same analysisVersion, the stored result is returned instead and `cached` is true (no new check is created); results are never shared between clients. A new result counts one unit of the client's monthly quota where plans are on (see `GET /api/v1/usage`); a cached one costs nothing. The listing is the marketplace's own format; for Etsy it is the Open API v3 style JSON with snake_case fields, for Amazon the simple format with title, brand, bullet_points, description, search_terms, product_type, price, quantity and images.

get.description:
Returns the numeric limits of the ruleset that `POST /api/v1/checks` applies to the marketplace, each with the field it applies to, the rule that enforces it, what it counts (`unit`), its severity, how well it is sourced and whether it is enabled. Every number comes from the loaded ruleset, so it is the number the check uses; use it for a character counter instead of copying the numbers. `rulesetVersion` is the version of the ruleset; when it changes, read the limits again.

For Amazon, `productType` applies that product type's override of the ruleset, as the check does; a product type with no override, and any product type for Etsy, gets the defaults. A rule that is switched off is listed with `enabled: false`. The answer is the same for every client, carries an `ETag` and may be cached for five minutes; it costs no quota and needs no plan pack. Call it from your backend: the API key must not be put in browser code.

parameters.description: Amazon product type whose override applies, for example `LUGGAGE`; matched ignoring case. Optional: without it, or with a product type that has no override, the defaults are returned.

post.description: Takes the same request as `POST /api/v1/checks` (`marketplace` and `listing` in the marketplace's own format), so a client can send one JSON to both endpoints. Compares the listing's text with the configured trademark catalog and returns findings with evidence: the field, the span in the text the API worked on (after trimming and Unicode NFC, UTF-16 offsets), the matched mark and how it matched. The result is a reference warning, not a legal conclusion; show the `disclaimer` with it. If the same client already sent the same listing text with the same analysisVersion and the stored result is complete and still retained, it is returned with `cached: true`. An INCOMPLETE result (a rule failed) is stored so its id can be read again, and is never reused for another request. A new complete result counts one unit of the client's monthly quota where plans are on (see `GET /api/v1/usage`); a cached or an INCOMPLETE one costs nothing. Results are kept for a limited time (`expiresAt`); only the listing's hash and the result are stored, not the listing text.

post.description: Takes a variation family: for Amazon a `parent` and its `children`, for Etsy the `variation_properties` and the `children` (see docs/input-schema.md, "Variation checks"). It is not the `/checks` envelope: a family is not a listing. Checks that the parent and its children are consistent (parent SKU, theme and its attributes, apparel size attributes, repeated combinations and SKUs, children that look like different products) and, for Etsy, the limits on variation types. The result is a reference warning built on secondary sources and internal heuristics, not a statement of the marketplace; show the `disclaimer` with it. It proposes no fix and no replacement value. If the same client already sent the same family with the same analysisVersion and the stored result is complete and still retained, it is returned with `cached: true`. An INCOMPLETE result (a rule failed) is stored so its id can be read again, and is never reused for another request. A new complete result counts one unit of the client's monthly quota where plans are on (see `GET /api/v1/usage`); a cached or an INCOMPLETE one costs nothing. Results are kept for a limited time (`expiresAt`); only the family's hash and the result are stored, not the family itself.

value.title: Too Many Requests

429.description: Two different answers, told apart by `code`. `rate-limited`: too many requests for the calling client (the same limit as the other endpoints); retry after the Retry-After header. `quota-exceeded` (only where plans are on): the month's quota of the client's plan is used up; there is no Retry-After, and retrying before `resetAt` does not help. A result already stored is still answered.

get.description: Returns the stored result of an earlier variation check of the calling client while it is retained, in the same shape as the POST response (`cached` is false). After `expiresAt`, for an unknown id and for another client's check the answer is the same 404.
